brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.evidence: One hex base piece (Hex base · North half, cell 0,0,level 0) is the only part placed. Its full base was swapped for a half base because drawers only attach to a base's cut face. Nothing else was added beside or on top of it; no covers, caps or bins.

The configurator offers a drawer only on the cut face of a half base, and a half base has one cut face, so a single base takes one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut). Five drawers would need several bases (or notch/bay parts beside touching bases), which breaks the single-base requirement. A full base offers no drawer sites at all.

finish.summary: Built one hex base (north half, so it has a cut face) with one drawer on that face. The configurator will not place five drawers on one base: drawers attach only to cut faces of half bases, and one base has only one such face. Meeting the five-drawer count needs more bases, which conflicts with the single-base brief, so I stopped at one drawer. Mesh check is clear. Open faces were left uncapped because you asked for nothing else added; the configurator notes three faces could take caps if you want them closed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
